title: Pressure at work
blurb: When work follows you home and won't let go.

days.title: Name it
days.read: Pressure gets heavier when it stays vague. Most of the weight comes from a few specific things, not "everything."
days.doThis: Write down the three things at work that are pressing on you most.
days.write: Which of the three can you actually change this week?

days.title: Your sphere
days.read: Some of it is yours to carry and some isn't. Carrying what isn't yours is where the exhaustion comes from.
days.doThis: Take one thing off your list that belongs to someone else, and hand it back.
days.write: What are you carrying that isn't yours?

days.title: One hard thing first
days.read: Dread grows the longer a task waits. Doing it early takes the air out of it.
days.doThis: Do your hardest task in the first hour tomorrow.
days.write: How did the rest of the day feel after?

days.title: Clock out
days.read: Your mind needs a clear end to the workday, or it never really stops.
days.doThis: Pick a time to stop tonight. Close the laptop and silence work alerts.
days.write: What did you do with the time you got back?

days.title: Talk to someone
days.read: Men often hold pressure in until it comes out sideways, at home or in the body.
days.doThis: Tell one person you trust how work is really going.
days.write: What changed when you said it out loud?

days.title: Move it out
days.read: Stress is a body thing as much as a mind thing. Movement burns it off.
days.doThis: Take a 20-minute walk after work, before you walk in the door.
days.write: How did you feel walking in after?

days.title: Who you are
days.read: Your job is what you do, not who you are. A bad week at work isn't a verdict on you.
days.doThis: Write one sentence about who you are that has nothing to do with work.
days.write: What would you want your kids or friends to say about you?

title: Anger and patience
blurb: For when your fuse is shorter than you want it to be.

days.title: Anger is a signal
days.read: Anger usually sits on top of something else: being tired, disrespected, afraid, or hurt.
days.doThis: Next time you feel it rise, ask: what's under this?
days.write: What was under your last flash of anger?

days.title: Your early warnings
days.read: Before you snap, your body tells you: jaw, shoulders, heat in the chest, a faster heartbeat.
days.doThis: Notice where anger shows up first in your body today.
days.write: Where did you feel it, and how early?

days.title: The 90-second pause
days.read: The first surge passes in about a minute and a half if you don't feed it.
days.doThis: When it rises, step away and breathe slowly for 90 seconds before you answer.
days.write: What happened when you paused?

days.title: Tired and hungry
days.read: A short fuse is often just low sleep, low food or too much caffeine.
days.doThis: Eat a real lunch and get to bed 30 minutes earlier tonight.
days.write: Was your patience different the next day?

days.title: Say it straight
days.read: Swallowing anger doesn't work either. It comes out later, bigger.
days.doThis: Tell someone calmly what bothered you, using "I felt" instead of "you always."
days.write: How did they respond?

days.title: Repair
days.read: Everyone loses it sometimes. What matters is coming back and making it right.
days.doThis: Go back to someone you snapped at and own your part.
days.write: What did repairing it cost you, and what did it give back?

days.title: Patience is a muscle
days.read: You get more patient the same way you get stronger: small reps, every day.
days.doThis: Pick one daily moment that tests you, and plan how you'll meet it.
days.write: What's your plan, in one line?

title: Becoming a dad
blurb: The first weeks and months, for you, not just the baby.

days.title: It's a lot
days.read: New dads get less sleep, less time and more worry, and are rarely asked how they are. About 1 in 10 get depressed after a birth.
days.doThis: Tell your partner or a friend one honest thing about how you're doing.
days.write: How are you, really?

days.title: Your part
days.read: Babies bond with whoever shows up: bathing, changing, rocking, holding them on your chest.
days.doThis: Take one feed, bath or bedtime on your own today.
days.write: What did you notice about your baby?

days.title: Care for her
days.read: Her body is healing and her hormones are crashing. What she needs most is rest and to be asked.
days.doThis: Ask her: what's one thing I can take off your plate today? Then do it.
days.write: What did she ask for?

days.title: Sleep in shifts
days.read: Two exhausted parents are worse than one rested one. Taking turns protects you both.
days.doThis: Agree a night shift plan so each of you gets one long stretch of sleep.
days.write: Did it work? What would you change?

days.title: Stay connected
days.read: Couples drift in the baby months without noticing. Ten minutes a day keeps you close.
days.doThis: Spend ten minutes together tonight without phones or baby talk.
days.write: What did you talk about?

days.title: Your body too
days.read: Dads stop moving, eat whatever and sleep badly. Small habits keep you able to show up.
days.doThis: Get a 15-minute walk in today, with the baby if you can.
days.write: How did you feel after?

days.title: The dad you want to be
days.read: You're already writing the story your kids will tell about you.
days.doThis: Write three words you want your kids to use about you one day.
days.write: What's one thing you can do this week that fits those words?

title: Purpose
blurb: For when you're going through the motions and want more.

days.title: Running on empty
days.read: Feeling flat isn't failure. It's often a sign you've drifted from what matters to you.
days.doThis: Write down when you last felt fully alive. What were you doing?
days.write: What made that moment different?

days.title: What you care about
days.read: Purpose starts with what you already care about, not something you have to invent.
days.doThis: List five things you care about deeply.
days.write: Which one gets the least of your time right now?

days.title: Your strengths
days.read: You're probably good at something you take for granted, because it comes easily.
days.doThis: Ask two people what they come to you for.
days.write: Did their answers surprise you?

days.title: Serve someone
days.read: Purpose shows up fastest when you use what you have for someone else.
days.doThis: Do one useful thing for someone today, without being asked.
days.write: How did it feel?

days.title: Small and daily
days.read: Purpose isn't one big decision. It's a daily direction you keep choosing.
days.doThis: Pick one small daily action that moves you toward what you care about.
days.write: What's your action?

days.title: Cut one thing
days.read: There's only so much room. Something has to go to make space.
days.doThis: Drop or cut back one thing that drains you and gives nothing back.
days.write: What did you cut?

days.title: Your sentence
days.read: A short sentence can steer a whole life.
days.doThis: Finish this: I'm here to...
days.write: Read it again. Does it sound like you?

title: Carrying everything
blurb: When you're the one who remembers it all, and you're worn out.

days.title: See the load
days.read: A lot of what tires you is invisible: remembering, planning, noticing, reminding. It counts as work even when nobody sees it.
days.doThis: Write down everything you kept track of today, for everyone. Don't leave anything out.
days.write: What on the list surprised you?

days.title: Not all yours
days.read: Some of it landed on you because you were the one who noticed. That doesn't make it yours forever.
days.doThis: Circle three things on your list that someone else could own completely.
days.write: Who could take each one?

days.title: Hand one over
days.read: Handing over means the whole job, including remembering it. If you still have to remind, you still carry it.
days.doThis: Give one task away today, start to finish. Then don't check on it.
days.write: What was hard about letting go?

days.title: Good enough
days.read: Done differently than you would do it is still done. Perfect is what keeps the load on your back.
days.doThis: Let one thing today be good enough, and leave it that way.
days.write: What happened when you left it?

days.title: Ask plainly
days.read: People close to you often can't see what you need. Hints don't work. Clear asks do.
days.doThis: Ask for one specific thing today: what, and by when.
days.write: How did they respond?

days.title: Rest without earning it
days.read: Rest isn't a prize for finishing. The list never finishes, so you'd never get any.
days.doThis: Take 20 minutes today for yourself with things still undone.
days.write: What did the guilt say, and was it true?

days.title: A lighter week
days.read: You can't drop everything, but you can change what a normal week holds.
days.doThis: Pick one thing to stop, one to share and one to keep. Tell someone your plan.
days.write: What will next week look like?

title: Comparison and enough
blurb: For when everyone else seems to be doing it better.

days.title: Notice it
days.read: Comparison is quick and quiet. You see a photo, a house, a body or a kid's report card, and you feel smaller.
days.doThis: Count how many times you compare yourself today. Just count.
days.write: When did it happen most?

days.title: Highlights only
days.read: You're comparing your whole life to the best minutes of someone else's. Nobody posts the hard parts.
days.doThis: Mute or unfollow three accounts that leave you feeling worse.
days.write: How did your day feel without them?

days.title: Your own lane
days.read: Her life has costs you can't see, and yours has good in it that she doesn't have.
days.doThis: Write five good things in your life you wouldn't trade.
days.write: Which one do you overlook most?

days.title: The mirror
days.read: Most women talk to themselves in a way they'd never talk to a friend.
days.doThis: Catch one harsh thought about your body or looks today, and say what you'd say to a friend.
days.write: What did you say instead?

days.title: Be glad for her
days.read: Someone else doing well takes nothing from you. Being glad for her breaks comparison faster than anything.
days.doThis: Tell one woman something you honestly admire about her.
days.write: How did it feel to say it?

days.title: Enough for today
days.read: You'll never get to the end of 'more.' Enough is something you decide, not something you reach.
days.doThis: Write down what enough looks like for you today, in one line.
days.write: Did you reach it?

days.title: Who you are
days.read: Your worth was settled before you did anything. It doesn't go up on good days or down on bad ones.
days.doThis: Write three things that are true about you that have nothing to do with how you look or what you get done.
days.write: Which one is hardest to believe?

title: Becoming a mom
blurb: The first weeks and months, for you, not just the baby.

days.title: It's a lot
days.read: Your body is healing, your sleep is broken and your whole life just changed. About 1 in 8 moms get depressed after a birth. If you feel low most days for two weeks, tell your doctor.
days.doThis: Tell one person an honest sentence about how you're doing.
days.write: How are you, really?

days.title: You're learning
days.read: Nobody knows how to do this at the start. You and your baby are learning each other, and it takes time.
days.doThis: Write one thing you can do now that you couldn't do a week ago.
days.write: What are you getting better at?

days.title: Accept help
days.read: When someone offers help, most new moms say they're fine. Help only works if you take it.
days.doThis: Say yes to one offer today, or ask for one specific thing.
days.write: What did you ask for?

days.title: Feed yourself too
days.read: You can't pour from empty. Food, water and a shower are part of caring for your baby.
days.doThis: Eat a real meal sitting down today, and keep water where you feed the baby.
days.write: What helped you most today?

days.title: Still you
days.read: You became a mother, and you're also still the person you were. She needs a little room too.
days.doThis: Do one small thing today that is only for you, even for ten minutes.
days.write: What did you choose?

days.title: Other moms
days.read: The loneliest part is thinking you're the only one finding it hard. You aren't.
days.doThis: Send one message to another mom and tell her something true.
days.write: What did she say back?

days.title: The mom you want to be
days.read: Your child won't remember a clean house. They'll remember how it felt to be with you.
days.doThis: Write three words you hope your child will use about you one day.
days.write: What's one small thing that fits those words?

title: Saying no without guilt
blurb: For when you say yes to everyone and have nothing left.

days.title: Where your yes goes
days.read: Every yes is paid for with time and energy you could have spent somewhere else.
days.doThis: List everything you said yes to this week. Mark the ones you didn't want to.
days.write: What did those yeses cost you?

days.title: Why it's hard
days.read: Saying no can feel unkind or selfish. Often it's a fear of letting people down or being thought less of.
days.doThis: Finish this sentence three times: If I say no, I'm afraid that...
days.write: Which fear is the loudest?

days.title: A small no
days.read: You build this the way you build any strength: start light.
days.doThis: Say no to one small thing today. No long reasons.
days.write: How did the other person take it?

days.title: Buy time
days.read: You don't have to answer on the spot. A pause protects you from a yes you'll regret.
days.doThis: Next time you're asked, say: let me check and get back to you.
days.write: What did you decide once you had time?

days.title: Guilt isn't proof
days.read: Feeling guilty doesn't mean you did wrong. It often just means you did something new.
days.doThis: When guilt shows up after a no, write down what you actually did wrong, if anything.
days.write: Was there anything on the list?

days.title: Limits are human
days.read: Nobody can be available to everyone all the time. The people who last are the ones who step away to rest.
days.doThis: Block one hour this week that belongs to nobody else.
days.write: What will you do with it?

days.title: Your best yes
days.read: A no to one thing is a yes to something that matters more.
days.doThis: Write the three things you most want to say yes to this season.
days.write: What needs a no so those can have a yes?
